name: runbook-k8s-restart
description: Restart a Kubernetes workload safely (rollout restart): a read-only baseline (rollout status, pods, restarts, events, the crashed containers' last logs - lost on restart), human approval, the restart with k8s_control (it waits for the rollout), then verification against the baseline. Fails, with the evidence, when the rollout does not complete healthy.

workload.description: deployment/<name>, statefulset/<name> or daemonset/<name> (or leave empty and give service).

service.description: An inventory service with a k8s mapping (instead of workload/namespace).

cluster.description: The inventory cluster (empty: the service's, or the only one).

precheck.title: Pre-checks (baseline)
precheck.prompt:
Pre-checks for a rollout restart of {{input.workload}} {{input.service}} (namespace {{input.namespace}}, cluster {{input.cluster}}; reason: {{input.reason}}). Read-only (kubernetes-triage skill): k8s_health for the workload (rollout status, revision, pods, restarts, events), k8s_logs for it with errors: true (the crashed containers' previous logs are lost on restart - keep the messages), and ops_inventory for maintenance windows.

Report: the baseline (desired/ready/available replicas, restarts, the problem lines), whether it is in a maintenance window, and whether a restart is likely to help - a crash loop from bad config or a bad image, or a Pending pod, will NOT be fixed by a restart: say so plainly.

restart.title: Restart
restart.prompt:
A person approved a rollout restart of {{input.workload}} {{input.service}} (namespace {{input.namespace}}, cluster {{input.cluster}}). Run k8s_control once with action restart and exactly that target (target = the workload, or service; namespace; cluster if given; reason "{{input.reason}}"), and nothing else.

Report: the tool's before/after output.

verify.title: Verify
